cues.en: I have a bit of a provocative title this year, but this is actually a talk that I've been giving for seven years in pieces. I'll explain what I mean by that. We are all here at CppCon and at conferences like it because we love C++. Maybe you feel as I do, C++ is the best language in the world for me to write the software I need and want to have. But C++ also has lots of challenges.
cues.zh: 今年我的标题有点挑衅，但这其实是我七年来分块讲的一个演讲。我会解释这是什么意思。我们都来到 CppCon 和类似会议，是因为我们热爱 C++。也许你和我一样觉得，C++ 是世界上最适合我编写自己需要和想要的软件的语言。但 C++ 也有很多挑战。

cues.en: And so we are in a phase where we are seeing the industry doing lots of major C++ evolution and sometimes revolution experiments. This talk is one of those. So I want to be clear up front, and I'll try to repeat it often. This is my personal experiment. I am not speaking for any company. I'm not speaking for the standards committee. It's my noodling around that I'm sharing.
cues.zh: 所以我们正处在一个阶段：业界正在进行大量重大的 C++ 演进，有时是革命性实验。这个演讲就是其中之一。所以我想一开始说清楚，并且我会尽量反复强调。这是我个人的实验。我不代表任何公司，也不代表标准委员会。这是我在分享自己的琢磨。

cues.en: because I hope it'll start a conversation in a direction to make C++ better. But if anything comes of this, well, first of all, it's an experiment, so it can fail. That's the default for experiments. And if anything does come of it, I intend to continue bringing those as ISO C++ proposals, and you'll see I've already been doing that. I would like to encourage us, as a community of 7 million C++ developers around the world, as we consider C++'s future,
cues.zh: 因为我希望它能开启一场让 C++ 变得更好的对话。但如果这真有什么成果，首先，它是个实验，所以可能失败。实验的默认结果就是失败。而如果真有什么成果，我打算继续把这些作为 ISO C++ 提案提交，你会看到我已经在这么做了。我想鼓励我们——作为全球 700 万 C++ 开发者组成的社区——在思考 C++ 的未来时，

cues.en: to push the boundaries to bring C++ itself forward and double down on C++, not be quick to switch to something else. To aim for major C++ evolution, 10x major, directed toward things that will make us better C++ programmers, not programmers of something else. And there are lots of good experiments going on and products. Rust is a real product, not in production, not in experiments. And there are other experiments.
cues.zh: 去突破边界，推动 C++ 本身前进，加倍投入 C++，而不是急于转向别的东西。要瞄准重大的 C++ 演进，10 倍级别，方向是让我们成为更好的 C++ 程序员，而不是别的语言程序员。现在有很多好的实验和产品。Rust 是真正的产品，不是还在生产环境里试用，也不是实验。而且还有其他实验。

cues.en: on that side of the range that do a greenfield language design, which is always fun to do, with new module systems, new packaging systems, building up their own new ecosystem, and those are valuable. And we can learn from them. But today, I'm talking about the other end of the spectrum. I am interested in refreshing C++ itself, making the guidance we already have, the modules we already have, the default.
cues.zh: 在那个方向上的另一端，有一些做全新语言设计的实验，这总是很有趣，带着新的模块系统、新的打包系统，建立自己的新生态，这些都很有价值。我们可以向它们学习。但今天，我谈的是光谱的另一端。我感兴趣的是刷新 C++ 本身，让我们已有的指南、已有的模块成为默认。

cues.en: keeping our ecosystem, our package managers, our full compatibility, but making C++ better. So here's a roadmap of what we're going to talk about. I'm going to talk about the motivation, the history that I've been working on this project for seven years now. So this is a bit of a coming out party, but you'll see I've already been talking about it for seven years. And we'll talk especially about safety and about simplicity examples.
cues.zh: 保持我们的生态、包管理器、完全兼容性，但让 C++ 更好。所以这是我们要讨论的路线图。我要讲动机，讲我从事这个项目七年的历史。所以这有点像一次正式亮相，但你会看到我已经谈了七年。我们尤其会讲安全性和简洁性的例子。

cues.en: And I'm always going to talk about metrics. So when you see on the right-hand side of this title card, every time it comes up as the roadmap, I'm interested in measurable progress. To me, 50x safer means 98% fewer CVEs, vulnerability exploits, and bugs in those categories. 10x simpler means I can get rid of 90% of the paper of the books I teach today. That's what I'm aiming for. What could go wrong?
cues.zh: 而且我总会谈指标。所以每次这张标题卡作为路线图出现时，你看右侧，我关心的是可衡量的进展。对我来说，安全 50 倍意味着 CVE、漏洞利用和这类 bug 减少 98%。简化 10 倍意味着我可以删掉今天所教书籍中 90% 的篇幅。这就是我的目标。能出什么错呢？

cues.en: So what is C++? This is a simplified version of a slide I showed here in 2018. That's CppCon. C++ is fundamentally about zero overhead abstraction. I always know where things are, how long they take, and friction-free interop backward compatibility. That is core. But the rest of this stuff, I mean, some people seem to think, if it doesn't hurt a little, it's not really C++. I challenge that.
cues.zh: 那么 C++ 是什么？这是我 2018 年在这里展示过的一张简化版幻灯片。那是 CppCon。C++ 的核心就是零开销抽象。我始终知道东西在哪、要花多久，以及无摩擦的互操作和向后兼容。这是核心。但其余那些，我是说，有些人似乎觉得，如果它不让人稍微痛点，就不算真正的 C++。我对此提出挑战。

cues.en: And we have been challenging that because specific syntax, we've been changing and adding syntax with every three-year release of the standard. Unsafe code, security exploits, those aren't core to the C++ experience, and we have been making those things better, but kind of like by 10% better-ish, every standard cycle. Not a game-changing 10x better. And the major reason for that, one major reason,
cues.zh: 我们一直在挑战这一点，因为具体语法，我们每三年发布一版标准时都在修改和增加语法。不安全代码、安全漏洞，这些都不是 C++ 体验的核心，我们一直在改善这些问题，但大概每个标准周期只好了 10% 左右。不是改变游戏规则的 10 倍提升。而主要原因，一个主要原因是，

cues.en: is that we have strictly hewn to 100% syntax, backward compatibility. What if we could have our cake and eat it too? And here is the strategy. The potential, if it works, judo move. You know our zero overhead principle we love so much? What if we applied that to backward source compatibility? That means we always have backwards 100% spinny macros, give us all of it.
cues.zh: 我们严格坚持 100% 语法向后兼容。如果我们能鱼与熊掌兼得呢？策略是这样。如果奏效，潜力会是一招柔道式借力。你知道我们深爱的零开销原则吧？如果我们把它应用到向后源代码兼容性上呢？这意味着我们始终有向后 100% 的兼容宏，全都给我们。

cues.en: backward source compatibility available, but we only pay for it if we use it. Is that possible? So I'm going to ask you to indulge me for the next hour and a half in a thought experiment backed by an implementation in the works. What could we do if we had a second syntax for C++? One of the things that would give us if it was a
cues.zh: 向后源代码兼容性随时可用，但我们只在使用它时才付出代价。这可能吗？所以接下来一个半小时，请容许我做一个思想实验，它背后有一个正在开发中的实现。如果我们为 C++ 准备第二套语法，能做什么？如果它是一套

cues.en: complete self-contained alternate syntax, had all the expressiveness, but spelled a different way than today, and it was unambiguous. That's a bubble of new code. You know what you have when you have a bubble of new code that doesn't exist today? Because nobody's written any code in the syntax yet today. You know what that means? You have exactly no backward source compatibility constraints. You can do anything you want that makes sense, that you feel is sensible,
cues.zh: 完整、自包含的替代语法，具备全部表达力，但写法与今天不同，而且没有歧义，这会给我们带来什么？那是一团新代码。你知道今天还不存在的一团新代码意味着什么吗？因为今天还没人用这套语法写过任何代码。你知道这意味着什么吗？你完全没有向后源代码兼容性约束。你可以做任何合理、你认为明智的事，

cues.en: without worrying about breaking code to reduce complexity, increase safety, improve toolability, and if it works out, to have a platform to build on to continue evolution for another 30 years. Remember when C++11 came out, there was no question it was still C++. But some of it looked a little foreign and fresh, like, oh, smart pointers. Oh, the left-to-right trailing return type declaration syntax.
cues.zh: 不必担心破坏代码，从而降低复杂度、提高安全性、改善工具支持，而且如果成功，还能有一个继续演进 30 年的平台。还记得 C++11 发布时吗？毫无疑问它仍然是 C++。但其中一些看起来有点陌生、有点新鲜，比如，哦，智能指针。哦，从左到右的尾置返回类型声明语法。

cues.en: Sure, we added stuff, but it was still C++. It felt like a new language. What if we could do that again for the whole language? That is what I've been working on primarily for the last seven years. So in 2015, I spent a year in copious free time as a lower priority than all the other work to say, could we refactor C++? I didn't start with a blank sheet and invent a language. That's fun, but that's not...
cues.zh: 当然，我们加了东西，但它仍然是 C++。感觉像一门新语言。如果我们能对整个语言再做一次这样的事呢？这就是我过去七年主要在做的事。2015 年，我花了大量业余时间，优先级低于所有其他工作，来问：我们能重构 C++ 吗？我并不是从白纸开始发明一门语言。那很好玩，但并不是……

cues.en: what I was interested in, I started with C++. What are the common pieces that may be spelled differently but could be unified? What are the pieces that we could refactor out so we have a smaller number of simpler, composable, general features that still let us express all the things we want to express, we're not dumbing it down, but the concept count is way lower. Because remember, concept count is the number of things you have to teach. And it's not just the number of keywords in a language, it's also the number of exceptions.
cues.zh: 我感兴趣的是，我从 C++ 开始。哪些常见部分虽然写法不同，但可以统一？哪些部分可以重构出去，从而用更少、更简单、可组合、通用的特性，仍能表达我们想表达的一切——不是把语言简化到变笨，而是概念数量大幅降低。因为记住，概念数量就是你必须教的东西的数量。它不只是语言里关键字的数量，还包括例外的数量。

cues.en: Any time you have an irregularity, any time you have two ways to say the same thing, any time you have, oh, but when these two features work together, something different happens. There's another thing to teach and another thing to teach. And you know what you get with that linear list? Rote learning. Rote learning is hard. That's why we want to reduce concept count. But you know, anything can look good on paper. So what I've been doing since 2016 is I've been taking one particular piece that could be disentangled
cues.zh: 每当你有一个不规则之处，每当你有两种方式说同一件事，每当遇到“哦，但这两个特性一起工作时，会发生不同的事”，就又有一个东西要教，又有一个东西要教。你知道这种线性清单会带来什么吗？死记硬背。死记硬背很难。这就是我们要降低概念数量的原因。但你知道，任何东西在纸面上都可能很好看。所以我从 2016 年以来一直在做的是，拿出某一个可以解耦的部分

cues.en: could be presented as a standalone proposal for ISO C++. And for the last six years, every conference talk I've given here and nearly every standards proposal paper I've written has come from the work I'm going to show you today just in today's syntax. And the reason is to flesh each one out because you get that next level of scrutiny so you find bugs and you can fix them.
cues.zh: 可以作为一个独立的 ISO C++ 提案提交。过去六年里，我在这里做的每一次会议演讲，以及我写的几乎每一篇标准提案论文，都来自我今天要用今天的语法展示的工作。原因是要把每一部分充实完善，因为这样你会得到下一层级的审视，从而发现 bug 并修好它们。

cues.en: And also validate, is this even a problem that the committee and you, the community, want to solve? Do you think it's important? And even if that's true, will you accept this solution direction, which is a separate question? This is all part of validating that there could be a there there. And so all of the proposals and talks and papers down at the bottom have come from this work. I want to call out one in particular, Spaceship, because of all of these, that's the only one I presented
cues.zh: 还要验证：这到底是不是委员会和你们、社区想要解决的问题？你们觉得它重要吗？就算重要，你们会接受这个解决方向吗？这又是另一个问题。这些都是验证“那里可能确实有东西”的一部分。所以下面所有的提案、演讲和论文都来自这项工作。我想特别指出一个：Spaceship，因为在所有这些当中，它是我唯一一个提交过

cues.en: and gave a paper without a prototype. And the reason is because I never actually had a talk about it here. I mentioned it for a few minutes in another talk because it was part of this design I had been doing, but it was a target of opportunity where after C++17 shipped, suddenly the committee continued talking about comparisons and it was clear that something was going to happen. So I thought, well, I have a design in my back pocket. Let me propose it. But it didn't have a prototype. And because of that, it had two major bugs.
cues.zh: 论文却没有原型的。原因是我实际上从未在这里专门讲过它。我在另一个演讲里提了几分钟，因为它是我一直在做的这个设计的一部分；但这是一个顺手的机会：C++17 发布后，委员会突然继续讨论比较，而且很明显会有事情发生。于是我想，好吧，我手头有一个现成的设计，让我提出来。但它没有原型。也正因如此，它有两个重大 bug。

cues.en: which were fixed thanks to these people. So I want to acknowledge them. Some of them are here in the room. If your picture is on the screen, would you please stand up and wave both your arms so people can see you? Some of you are way at the back, some of you are at the front. And give them a round of applause, please. Thank you so much. And of course, others, many others helped too. It's a large committee. This is the first piece of my simplification work that is part of the standard. And I think that's the right path to go.
cues.zh: 这些 bug 多亏这些人修好了。所以我想感谢他们。有些人就在这个房间里。如果你的照片在屏幕上，请站起来挥动双臂，让大家看到你，好吗？你们有些人坐在很后面，有些人在前面。请给他们一轮掌声。非常感谢。当然，还有其他人，很多人也帮了忙。这是一个很大的委员会。这是我的简化工作中第一块进入标准的部分。我认为这是正确的方向。

cues.en: And I brag on Spaceship a little because it's the first feature we've ever added to C++ where, yes, you added a dozen pages for the core language wording, but it made the standard smaller because we applied it in the library and it reduced more than that many pages in the standard library. So I take that as some data that, yes, simplifying can work. But now let's talk about...
cues.zh: 我吹一下 Spaceship 操作符，因为它是我们加入 C++ 的第一个新特性，虽然核心语言规范增加了十几页，但它让整个标准变薄了，因为标准库用上它之后减掉的页数还要多得多。这证明了：是的，做减法、做简化是行得通的。不过现在我们来谈谈……

cues.en: the problem. I already talked about the problem of prototyping. The biggest thing that's been holding me back is it is expensive to prototype things in a production C++ compiler. Some of these have been my own little library, some have been done in Clang, some have been done in Visual Studio. But man, it's expensive to do. So then I thought, as we all should, wait for it. What would Bjarne do? But not this Bjarne. Not this Bjarne.
cues.zh: ……真正的问题。我刚才聊到了做原型的难题。一直阻碍我的最大障碍是：在一个生产级的 C++ 编译器里做原型成本太高了。其中有些是我自己的小库，有些是在 Clang 里做的，有些是在 Visual Studio 里做的。但是天哪，做起来成本真的太高了。于是我就想——大家应该都会这么想，等一下——Bjarne 会怎么做？但不是这位 Bjarne。不是这位。

cues.en: Other Bjarne in this picture, that Bjarne. It's a cardboard cutout, but the picture works, so I'm going to go with it. What would that Bjarne do? And the really nice thing about asking a question of what would somebody 40 years ago do is you could look it up on Wikipedia if they succeeded. And that's why we're all here. What Bjarne did is he built C front. It was a C++ compiler that emitted C code.
cues.zh: 而是照片里的另一位 Bjarne，那个 Bjarne。虽然只是个人形立牌，但这图挺合用，就用它吧。那个 Bjarne 会怎么做？问“40年前的人会怎么做”最大的好处在于，你可以去维基百科查查他们最后有没有成功。而这正是我们今天齐聚一堂的原因。Bjarne 当年做的是构建了 Cfront。那是一个生成 C 代码的 C++ 编译器。

cues.en: And if you weren't around in the 80s, as many of us weren't in computing, you may forget that for the first decade of C++'s life, this was the C++ compiler, and C with classes, before it was even called C++. And Bjorna nailed three things. He nailed his value proposition, but he had a 15-second elevator speech. We love C. It's powerful, machine-near, flexible, but it needs abstraction. I'm going to solve that problem.
cues.zh: 如果你在80年代还没涉足计算机——我们很多人当时都还没入行——你可能会忘了，在 C++ 诞生的头十年里，以及在它还被称为“带类的 C（C with Classes）”、甚至还没叫 C++ 之前，这就是当时唯一的 C++ 编译器。Bjarne 做成了三件事。他明确了自己的价值主张，而且有一段15秒的电梯演讲：我们热爱 C，它强大、贴近硬件、灵活，但它需要抽象能力。我要来解决这个问题。

cues.en: That's a succinct elevator pitch. And by compiling to C, it meant it was available wherever a C compiler was available. And you had full interoperability with C code, with C optimizers, linkers, debuggers, tools. Yeah, in the debugger, you might see a mangled name for certain for an overloaded function, but the debugger worked. This was powerful for C++'s early adoption. Without C front, we wouldn't be here. So my experiment is,
cues.zh: 这是个非常精练的电梯演讲。而且通过编译成 C，意味着只要有 C 编译器的地方就能使用它。你能与 C 代码、C 优化器、链接器、调试器以及各类工具完全互操作。没错，在调试器里，重载函数的名称可能会被修饰（mangled），但调试器确实能正常工作。这对 C++ 早期的推广起到了巨大作用。没有 Cfront，就没有我们的今天。所以我的实验是：

cues.en: Could we do that again? And what I'm about to present is just my own experiment, my own personal code. It is live on GitHub under hsutter. You can find it at Cppfront. It is a syntax2 to syntax1 compiler in progress. But I have similar goals to Bjarne's. I love C++. Let's embrace C++ and double down on it, but address that it needs to be safer, simpler, and more toolable.
cues.zh: 我们能不能再复制一次？接下来我要展示的，仅仅是我自己的实验和个人代码。它已经在 GitHub 上的 hsutter 账号下公开，项目名叫 cppfront。它是一个正在开发中的 syntax2 到 syntax1 的编译器。但我有着与 Bjarne 相似的目标。我热爱 C++。让我们拥抱并加倍押注 C++，但同时解决它需要更安全、更简单、对工具更友好的问题。

cues.en: Those are the problems we want to solve, but we still want it to be C++. And it works wherever a C++ 20 compiler is available. You'll see that in live demos today. And have full interoperability with today's C++. It should be C++, just nicer. Caveats, again, my personal experiment. Have I said that enough times now? This is a partial compiler, hilariously incomplete. Over the winter, I hope to add classes.
cues.zh: 这些就是我们要解决的问题，但我们依然希望它保持是 C++。只要有支持 C++20 的编译器，它就能运行——今天你们会在现场演示中看到。而且它能与当下的 C++ 完全互操作。它应该还是 C++，只是体验更好。再次声明，这只是我的个人实验，我说得够多次了吧？它还是个未完成的编译器，甚至不完整得有些可笑。今年冬天，我希望能把类（classes）的功能加进去。

cues.en: I mean, it's hilariously incomplete. Turns out you can get a lot of simplification just from functions. But my hope here is to start a conversation. Before we rush off to a different language, what could be possible within C++'s own evolution to rejuvenate C++? So here are the complete build instructions for CPP front. One line for each major compiler. The builds and runs today are all major compilers in C++ 20 mode.
cues.zh: 我是说，它不完整得好笑。结果发现，光靠函数就能带来大量简化。但我这里的希望是开启一场讨论。在我们急着转向另一门语言之前，在 C++ 自身演进中，有哪些可能让 C++ 焕发新生？所以这里是 CPP front 的完整构建说明。每个主流编译器一行。今天的构建和运行都覆盖所有主流编译器，使用 C++20 模式。

cues.en: When you write your own code in the syntax2, CPP2, I call it for short, which can be either a file that's all CPP2 syntax or that's interleaved with today's syntax and the second one, then just run it through CPP front and then that will produce a CPP file, which you then just run through your compiler.
cues.zh: 当你用 syntax2（我简称 CPP2）写自己的代码时，它可以是一个全 CPP2 语法的文件，也可以是一个与现行语法交错的文件；后一种情况下，把它交给 CPP front 跑一遍，就会生成一个 CPP 文件，然后你再把它交给编译器。

cues.en: So the top half of this slide is the complete build instructions. There is no Bazel, there's no CMake, there's no third-party library dependencies, there's no Yak or Bison because I started with an empty editor and the standard library, and I never looked back so far. There's no third-party code, it's a custom-written manual parser, and all the code is custom-written by me. Let me just talk a little bit about an important principle and stakes in the ground.

cues.en: that says it's the same type as string, so the deduced type is string. You can do this today, but almost nobody does. This is how you forward a concrete type. Normally, perfect forwarding only works for template parameter types. You might have noticed those symbols at the bottom.
cues.zh: 这个子句表示它和 string 是同一种类型，所以推导出的类型就是 string。现在你就可以这么做，但几乎没人这么做。这就是转发具体类型的方法。通常，完美转发只适用于模板参数类型。你也可以那样做，但现在还可以轻松转发具体类型，然后我们会自动从明确的最后一次使用处进行转发，就像底部看到的那样。还有最后一点，你可能注意到了底部的那些符号。

cues.en: I've talked about consistency in functions. There's one way to declare functions in CPP2. This is my experiment anyway. A named function just has a name in front of the colon. The exact same function can be written at expression scope as an argument to std ranges for each. We call it a lambda today, but I think of it as just a function expression. It's just still the same grammar. It goes through the same function in my parser. And a range for loop body.
cues.zh: 我之前讲过函数的一致性。在 CPP2 中，函数只有一种声明方式。至少这是我的尝试。命名函数只需要把名称放在冒号前面。同一个函数也可以在表达式作用域中写成传给 std ranges for each 的参数。我们现在把它叫作 lambda，但我更愿意把它看成一个函数表达式。它仍然使用相同的语法，也会经过解析器中的同一个函数。范围 for 循环体也一样。

cues.en: is also a function, because that's the one place in the language with the semantics of that we invoke some code repeatedly with some arguments that change, sort of range for loop does. The syntax is the same. And if you've been hearing me all hour and a half long saying how the syntaxes are all the same, how many of you have wondered, yeah, but what about capture? Come on, it's OK. A few. So you think, oh, Herb's oversimplifying, because you need lambda capture, right?
cues.zh: 它同样是一个函数，因为在这门语言里，只有这里的语义是：我们会用一些不断变化的参数，反复调用一段代码，这正是范围 for 循环所做的。语法也是一样的。如果你听了我整整一个半小时，一直在说所有语法都一样，那么有多少人会想：没错，但捕获怎么办？别担心，没关系，确实有几个人这么想。所以你会觉得，Herb 这是在过度简化，因为 lambda 需要捕获，对吧？

cues.en: Yeah, you do. But you don't necessarily need a different function declaration syntax to do it. And I have to credit Tim Sweeney with this. I was sitting with Tim Sweeney in his offices a few years ago, talking about this. And he said, well, for Lambda, why don't you just always capture in the body? And by the way, always capture by value. If you want a pointer, take the address and capture that. And especially now that I have pointer safety and initialization safety, that made a lot of sense to me. So thank you.
cues.zh: 是的，确实可以。但你不一定需要另一套函数声明语法来实现这一点。这一点我要感谢 Tim Sweeney。几年前，我在 Tim Sweeney 的办公室和他聊这件事。他说，Lambda 为什么不直接总是在函数体中捕获呢？而且，顺便说一句，始终按值捕获。如果你需要指针，就获取它的地址，然后捕获这个地址。尤其是现在我已经有了指针安全和初始化安全，这对我来说就很有道理了。所以，谢谢你。

cues.en: Tim, I took that one and ran with it. So I appreciate it. So this is how Lambda capture looks. And it's only allowed inside expression functions, but it's the same grammar. It's just restricted outside expressions. If I want S's value, I capture it there, and then later when the Lambda's invoked, I use the value. Can you think of any other place in current or currently proposed C++ that is like capture?
cues.zh: Tim，我采纳了这个想法并继续推进，真的很感谢。所以，Lambda 捕获就是这样写的。它只允许出现在表达式函数中，但使用的是同一套语法，只是函数体外的表达式受到限制。如果我想要 S 的值，就在那里捕获它；之后调用 Lambda 时，再使用这个值。你能想到当前 C++ 或正在提议中的 C++ 里，还有什么地方也类似于捕获吗？

cues.en: that is kind of like this, where you capture something and then execute it later. Co-routines, that's a good one. Anything else? There's a few. The one I was thinking of is post conditions. So this code works in Cpp2 today, the code at top. A post condition, you often want to look at the initial value. So I thought, well, the post condition, you write it at the top of the function, which is conceptually on enter, right? And you execute it when you leave the function, not through an exception. On return,
cues.zh: 也就是捕获某个东西，然后稍后执行它。协程，这是一个很好的例子。还有吗？其实还有几个。我想到的是后置条件。所以，顶部这段代码现在在 Cpp2 中就能运行。后置条件通常需要查看初始值。所以我想，后置条件应该写在函数顶部，从概念上说就是进入函数时，对吧？然后在离开函数时执行，而不是通过异常执行。在返回时，

cues.en: at the end or a return in the middle. So what I'll do is that's capture. If I want to say for a pushback, pushback one value, that the post condition is that the new collection size is the old collection size plus one, well, I'll just capture the old collection size here, or say collection size capture. And then when the post condition is evaluated at the end, collection size equals that captured value plus one, works great. And if you're familiar with other languages in one other place,
cues.zh: 无论是在末尾返回，还是在中途返回。所以我会把这当作捕获。如果我要表达的是，对于一次 pushback，添加一个值后，后置条件应当是新集合大小等于旧集合大小加一，那么我只需在这里捕获旧的集合大小，或者说捕获 collection size。然后在函数末尾评估后置条件时，collection size 等于捕获的值加一，这就很好用了。如果你熟悉其他语言，还能想到另一个使用场景，

cues.en: which is string interpolation. All three of them, this code works today in CPP2, they all use the same syntax. And I think it's really important that there's one way to capture, there's one way to declare functions, there's one way to declare anything, because variables, types, and functions are all declared the same way. And then we can get on with writing the business logic that we want, that we get paid to do. So we've talked about all these things, and I want to make an observation here at the end.
cues.zh: 那就是字符串插值。这三种情况，在 CPP2 中今天都能运行，它们使用同一种语法。我认为，只有一种捕获方式、只有一种函数声明方式，以及只有一种声明其他内容的方式，这一点非常重要，因为变量、类型和函数都用同样的方式声明。这样我们就能专心编写真正想写、也是我们靠它谋生的业务逻辑了。我们已经讨论了这些内容，最后我想指出一点。

cues.en: Think about the words and the ideas that we've been using for the last hour and a half. I have not said the word monad once. All of the words and the ideas that we have been using are not weird foreign terms from some other language, not weird foreign concepts from some other language. They are things we are deeply familiar with. They're how we talk. They're how we think. And I want that.
cues.zh: 想想过去一个半小时里我们一直在使用的词语和概念。我一次都没有提到过“单子”这个词。我们使用的所有词语和概念，都不是来自其他语言的奇怪外来术语，也不是来自其他语言的奇怪外来概念。它们都是我们非常熟悉的东西，是我们的表达方式，也是我们的思考方式。我希望如此。

And longer term, if you're interested in taking an existing major C++ compiler's pretty printer and emitting Cpp2 code, so I call that front Cpp,
cues.zh: Cpp2draw，如果你对带键盘和文本的基础绘图 API 感兴趣，基本上就是 21 世纪的 Curses 或 Conio.h，尤其是如果你能想到办法让它做成 header-only，请给我发邮件。更长期地，如果你有兴趣拿现有主流 C++ 编译器的 pretty printer 来输出 Cpp2 代码，我把它叫作 front Cpp，

Because one of the things that could do is in today's code, detect patterns and idioms that in CPP2 can be expressed directly and translate them. So that's a source migration tool. That's a longer term project idea. But let me close with this. What if we could do C++ feels like a new language again, like we did in C++11? Feels like it, but it is still C++.
cues.zh: 这名字似乎挺合理，发邮件给我。因为它能做的一件事，是在今天的代码里检测那些在 Cpp2 中可以直接表达的模式和惯用法，并把它们翻译过来。所以那是一个源码迁移工具。那是一个更长期的项目想法。但让我这样收尾。如果我们能让 C++ 再次感觉像一门新语言，像 C++11 那样，会怎样？感觉像，但它仍然是 C++。

cues.en: but this time do it broadly across the whole language. This is an experiment that can fail. If somebody can find a better way to skin this cat, please do. I want to start a conversation to see if we can try it out, to see if we could get there. The idea would be to support, not compete with C++ evolution, embrace C++ 20, 23, 26, embrace the modules we have, make import std the default. Think of it.
cues.zh: 但这次要在整个语言范围内广泛地做。这是一个可能失败的实验。如果有人能找到更好的办法做这件事，请尽管去做。我想开启一场对话，看看我们能否试一试，看看我们能否走到那里。这个想法是支持而不是与 C++ 演进竞争，拥抱 C++20、23、26，拥抱我们已有的模块，让 import std 成为默认。想想看。

cues.en: I do as a directed evolution of C++ itself, and compiling to today's C++ keeps us honest. And then as we learn things, we can bring parts of the whole thing to ISO C++ because they own the language. That is what C++ is. So here are the major things that I talked about today. And just to put it in perspective, let's look at what are the things that I hope, and if this succeeds,
cues.zh: 我确实把它看作 C++ 自身的一种定向演化，而编译到今天的 C++ 能让我们保持诚实。然后随着我们学到东西，可以把整体中的部分带回 ISO C++，因为他们拥有这门语言。C++ 就是这样。所以这些是我今天谈到的主要东西。为了有个全局视角，让我们看看我希望能做到的事情，以及如果这成功了，

cues.en: I hope I never have to teach or think about anymore. Some things just go away, so there's nothing in the CPP2 column. There's no preprocessor, so I don't have to teach include, which standard header to include, ordering dependencies, four declarations, those just go away. My one declaration syntax gets rid of the vexing parse, East versus West cons, but you can still wear the bracelets. The inside out declarations, all the different member function versus non-member versus lambda syntax as we have, et cetera.
cues.zh: 我希望自己再也不必教或思考这些东西。有些东西直接消失，所以 Cpp2 那一栏里什么都没有。没有预处理器，所以我不必教 include、该包含哪个标准头、顺序依赖、前置声明，这些统统消失。我这一套声明语法消除了 most vexing parse、East const 与 West const 之争，但你仍然可以戴手镯（花括号）。由内而外的声明，以及我们现有的成员函数、非成员函数、lambda 等所有不同语法，等等。

cues.en: The incopy in out and out get rid of, do I pass x or const ref x? If I pass a value or value const parameter, why are those really the same thing except when they're not? What about references? And I would like to just get rid of references throughout the language because they were only designed for parameter passing. That's why we already introduced them in the language.
cues.zh: in、copy、inout 和 out 消除了这些问题：我该传 x 还是 const ref x？如果我传值或 value const 参数，为什么它们其实是一回事，除非又不是？引用呢？我甚至想在整个语言中去掉引用，因为它们最初只是为参数传递设计的。这正是我们当初把它们引入语言的原因。

cues.en: but they're put through the whole type system, so we constantly have to answer questions about them. That makes the language more complex, even when we're not using references in many of those other contexts. Move, std move, why it doesn't move, why it's overused, why not to return std move, why ref ref isn't actually an rvalue reference if the type is a template parameter type, and then forward, std forwards, how to spell perfect forwarding.
cues.zh: 但它们会贯穿整个类型系统，所以我们得不断回答关于它们的问题。这让语言变得更复杂，即使我们在很多其他场景中并不使用引用。移动、std::move、为什么它没有移动、为什么它被滥用、为什么不该返回 std::move、为什么当类型是模板参数类型时，ref ref 实际上并不是右值引用；还有 forward、std::forward，以及完美转发该怎么写。

cues.en: That is not something I would teach a regular C++ class. Well, a forwarding reference is only for template types, how to forward a non-template type. Named return values. Did you notice that you automatically, when you get the named return values I showed, NRVO just falls out because you're always returning that same name. So you automate NRVO as well.
cues.zh: 这不是我会在普通 C++ 课程里讲的内容。比如，转发引用只适用于模板类型；非模板类型该怎么转发？命名返回值。你注意到了吗？当你使用我刚才展示的命名返回值时，NRVO 会自动发生，因为你始终返回的是同一个名字。这样你也自动获得了 NRVO。

cues.zh: 我正在尝试验证这一点，看看能不能通过真正实现它来证明，因为我热爱 C++。对我来说，目前它是编写自己需要和想要编写的代码的世界上最好的语言。但我希望能把代码写得更优雅一些。我也想看看这个实验能否成功，或者能否有人受到这个实验的启发，做得更好。五年后，十年后，我们能不能拥有这样的 C++：

cues.en: we can be writing C++ with a lot more certainty, with a lot less to teach and learn, with a lot more simplicity, with the same kind of tools other languages enjoy. Do you think that's an experiment worth doing? Is that something you would like to see happen? We have time for one or two questions if you want to line up at the mics, and we might have one online. We'll just keep right at time, but we'd like to take one or two.
cues.zh: 我们可以更有把握地编写 C++，需要教授和学习的内容少得多，语言更加简单，同时拥有其他语言所享有的同类工具。你觉得这是一个值得进行的实验吗？你希望看到它实现吗？如果你想来麦克风前提问，我们还有时间回答一两个问题，线上可能也有一个问题。我们会严格控制时间，但希望能回答一两个问题。

cues.en: Hello, Herb. Maybe I'll take one here, one here, and then online. I apologize. Yes. I don't really have a question, but I just wanted to let everyone in the room know that as of a few moments ago, Matt added support for CPP Front to Compiler Explorer. Thank you, Matt. You're my hero. And to be clear, you've been my hero for years. Thank you for Compiler Explorer. OK, that doesn't count as a question. One more over here. Thank you, Matt.
cues.zh: 你好，Herb。也许我先回答这边一个，这边一个，然后再看线上的。抱歉。好的。我其实没有提问，只是想告诉在场的大家，就在刚才，Matt 在 Compiler Explorer 中加入了对 CPP Front 的支持。谢谢你，Matt。你就是我的英雄。顺便澄清一下，你很多年前就已经是我的英雄了。感谢你做出 Compiler Explorer。好的，这可不算提问。这边还有一个。谢谢 Matt。

cues.en: Hey, thank you so much. I just wanted to ask, not because it so matters to me, but because C++ is the zero over the abstraction language to me. But some of the abstractions that CPP2 introduces is like the deferred initialization, which has probably a Boolean, which introduces over it even to types like integer. So I wonder, how do you pretend to tackle all this versus the concept of zero over the abstraction?
cues.zh: 嘿，非常感谢。我只是想问一下，倒不是说这对我有多重要，而是因为对我来说 C++ 是一门零开销抽象的语言。但 CPP2 引入的一些抽象，比如延迟初始化，可能会带一个布尔值，这甚至会对像整型这样的类型引入额外开销。所以我想知道，面对零开销抽象这个概念，你打算如何解决这些问题？

cues.en: Yes, so the zero overhead principle isn't zero cost, so you don't pay for what you don't use. So absolutely, first of all, my answer to all such questions is, it's an experiment. Experiments can fail. So we're going to learn by trying. We should try. My second answer in this particular case is, you don't pay for it unless you use it. 90% of the time, you should just give an initial value when you declare the variable. That's zero overhead.
cues.zh: 是的，零开销原则并不是零成本，而是“不用则不付费”。所以毫无疑问，首先我对所有这类问题的回答都是：这是一个实验。实验可能会失败。所以我们要边做边学，我们应该去尝试。针对这个具体情况，我的第二个回答是：除非你用了，否则你不需要为此买单。90% 的情况下，你只要在声明变量时给它赋个初始值就行了。那就是零开销。

cues.en: If you choose to defer initialization, maybe because you want to call a different constructor on different branches, or on this branch you want to call a constructor, and on this one you have to call a function that will do the work, then you might would get the extra Boolean, but you only pay for what you use. That's the principle. And it's an experiment, so we'll see how well it works. But a good observation. Yeah, thanks for the answer. Can I follow up on this? If it's quick, and then we'll take one more. Okay, so...
cues.zh: 如果你选择延迟初始化，可能是因为你想在不同分支调用不同的构造函数，或者在这个分支你想调用构造函数，而在那个分支你必须调用一个函数来完成工作，那这时你可能会多引入一个布尔值，但你只为你使用的东西买单。这就是原则。而且这是一个实验，我们拭目以待它的效果。不过你观察得很敏锐。好的，谢谢解答。我能追问一下吗？如果很快的话可以，然后我们再接一个问题。好的，那就是……

cues.en: One of the things you also added is basically avoiding union and using std variant. This also kind of introduces overheads. I'm just looking for the parts where people who want to take control and want the zero over it, they can't because of these rules enforcement. Yeah, so that's a reasonable question. So today we already teach people don't use union, use std variant instead. So we're already teaching that. I didn't make that up here. If you really want union,
cues.zh: 你加入的另一件事基本上是避免使用 union，转而使用 std::variant。这某种程度上也引入了开销。我只是想知道，对于那些想要完全掌控、想要零开销的人，他们是否会因为这些强制规则而无法实现？是的，问得很有道理。其实现在我们已经在教大家别用 union，改用 std::variant 了。我们已经在这么教了，并不是我在这里凭空编出来的。如果你真的想用 union，

cues.en: We have full backward source compatibility always available. You pay for it only if you use it. You can write union still in the CPP2 file because we still have CPP1 syntax. It's all still there. Thank you. It seems clear that a big part of your goal here is to make it harder to write bad code, make the default behavior better. One thing I noticed while you were demonstrating is
cues.zh: 我们一直提供完全的源码向后兼容性。你只在用到它时才付出代价。你仍然可以在 CPP2 文件里写 union，因为我们仍保留了 CPP1 语法。它们都还在。谢谢。看起来很明显，你的很大一部分目标就是让写出糟糕的代码变得更难，让默认行为变得更好。你在演示的时候我注意到了一件事：

cues.en: Why is dash P not default behavior for your compiler? So why is dash P not the default behavior for the compiler? It stands for dash pure CPP2. Because I want to allow mixed code. Because dash P means you can only write in CPP2. You can't use include, you can't use macros, or anything like that. So why not make mixed code the one you have to put a flag for? Yeah, we could do that too.
cues.zh: 为什么 -p 不是编译器的默认行为呢？那么为什么 -p 不是编译器的默认行为？它代表纯粹的 CPP2。因为我想允许混合代码。因为 -p 意味着你只能写 CPP2，不能用 include，不能用宏，或者任何类似的东西。那为什么不把混合代码做成需要额外加参数的形式呢？嗯，我们也可以这么做。

cues.en: But let me generalize your question a bit. The reason some of those others are, for instance, subscript checking and null deref checking, those are two switches. The reason they're opt-in is because I conjecture they're probably pretty cheap for various memory architecture reasons and the way branch predictors work, but I don't know. They might have non-negligible overhead, so I put them under a switch for now to make them opt-in. But we'll learn as we go. I hope to learn a lot. Do we have any online? Yes.
cues.zh: 不过我先把你这个问题说得更宽泛一点。其中有些检查，比如下标检查和空指针解引用检查，是两个开关。它们之所以按需启用，是因为我推测，出于各种内存架构方面的原因以及分支预测器的工作方式，它们可能开销很低，但我并不确定。它们可能有不可忽视的开销，所以目前我把它们放在开关下面，让它们按需启用。不过我们会边做边学。我希望学到很多。线上有人吗？有。

cues.en: This is a question from Alexi. What is your idea for things that still require the preprocessor now? Specifically, I mean line file function. I'd love to have a logging statement or an exception check without having to use a macro. C++23 has the source location, but you'd still need a macro in order to capture the current line. Yes. So in general,
cues.zh: 这是 Alexi 的问题。对于那些目前仍然需要预处理器的东西，你有什么想法？具体来说，我指的是行号、文件、函数。我很想在不使用宏的情况下拥有日志语句或异常检查。C++23 有 source_location，但为了捕获当前行，你仍然需要宏。是的。所以总的来说，

cues.en: We're currently working our way through trying to figure out how to get rid of the uses of the preprocessor. Modules are a huge step in that direction. Constexpr is another huge step in that direction. There are a few things left, such as Poundline, which I use in CppFront to omit the code, to line up the diagnostics correctly with the original source file. So the goal is to work through that tail and to have replacements
cues.zh: 我们目前正在努力弄清楚如何摆脱对预处理器的使用。模块是朝这个方向迈出的一大步。constexpr 是朝这个方向迈出的又一大步。还剩下几件事，比如 #line，我在 CppFront 里用它来省略代码，让诊断信息与原始源文件正确对齐。所以目标是处理完这条尾巴，并准备好替代方案，

cues.en: for all of the things that currently require macros. One of the things I hope that will get us the next big step there is by having reflection and generation because that gets rid of a lot of the remaining use cases I know of where I resort to macros today. Good question. Okay, one more and then we'll close. I think you'll like this one. So there's a lot of teaching that is difficult because of the things we can't put in the books.
cues.zh: 用于所有目前需要宏的东西。我希望带我们迈出下一步的其中一件事，是拥有反射和生成，因为这会消除我知道的许多目前仍要依赖宏的用例。好问题。好，再问一个然后我们就结束。我觉得你会喜欢这个。有很多教学之所以困难，是因为有些东西我们没法写进书里。

cues.en: Oh, it's like I paid you to ask this question. It's not just things we would like to take out. So why not have standard file extensions, standard formatting, standard variable naming conventions, and things like that? I am a big fan of constraints. Constraints are liberating. To use the frequent quote, constraints are liberating because they focus ingenuity in the directions that matter. I'm not convinced those matter.
cues.zh: 哦，简直像是我花钱请你问这个问题。这不只是我们想拿掉的东西。那为什么不要标准文件扩展名、标准格式化、标准变量命名约定之类的东西呢？我非常喜欢约束。约束带来自由。用那句常被引用的话说，约束带来自由，因为它们把创造力集中到真正重要的方向上。我不确定这些是否重要。

cues.en: Some of them may, but naming conventions... One of the things that I mentioned on the slides that I'm taking as a stake in the ground, there are many improvements I think I could make, but I can't justify by saying it would remove X percent of CVEs. It would remove X percent of items in a coding standard book or in an effective C++ book. If you can convince me that a naming convention for variables
cues.zh: 其中一些可能重要，但命名约定……我在幻灯片里提到的一件事，是我作为基本立场提出的一点：我认为我可以做很多改进，但我无法用“它能消除 X% 的 CVE”来证明。它能去掉编码标准书或《Effective C++》里 X% 的条目。如果你能说服我，针对变量的命名约定

cues.en: would get rid of like 5% of the things that we currently teach people, now you've got my attention. But I would need to be able to prove that and measure it. But they do add a lot of complexity to the tooling ecosystem, right? Because we have to have tools that, like all these different formators, and they can't just deduce that, well, you named it this way, so it should probably be const, and you named it wrong, and things like that, right? OK. So let me answer that, and then springboard to a second topic.
cues.zh: 能去掉我们目前教给人们的大约 5% 的内容，那你就引起我的注意了。但我需要能够证明并衡量这一点。不过它们确实会给工具生态增加很多复杂性，对吧？因为我们必须有工具，比如所有这些不同的格式化工具，而它们不能只是推断：好吧，你这样命名，所以它大概应该是 const，而你命名错了，诸如此类，对吧？好。那我来回答这个问题，然后借此跳到第二个话题。

cues.en: One of the reasons tools need those heuristics is because it's so hard to write a C++ parser. In the CPP front repo, I have written so far only a partial, but a standalone context-free, order-independent parser that I hope to grow to have the same expressiveness as the full C++ syntax we have today, and a parser people can reuse. Once you have that, you have to lean on heuristics less.
cues.zh: 工具需要这些启发式方法的原因之一，是写 C++ 解析器太难了。在 CPP front 仓库里，我目前只写了一个不完整的解析器，但它是独立的、上下文无关、顺序无关的解析器；我希望它能发展到和今天完整的 C++ 语法同样有表现力，并成为人们可以复用的解析器。一旦有了它，就不必那么依赖启发式方法了。

cues.en: So that's one thing to say, but you reminded me of one last thing, so I'll close on this thought. So thank you for that. One of the things that really bugs Bjarne and me and others is people teaching C++ starting with C. But that's an artifact of the fact that backward source compatibility is always mandatory. They do it because they can, because that code works.
cues.zh: 这是其中一点，但你让我想起最后一件事，我就以这个想法收尾。谢谢你提醒我。真正让 Bjarne 和我以及其他一些人困扰的一件事，是人们教 C++ 时从 C 开始。但这是“向后源码兼容始终是强制要求”这一事实的产物。他们这么做是因为可以这么做，因为那些代码能跑。

cues.en: That's why so many colleges and universities still teach fprintf early in a C++ course, which isn't bad, but it's not C++, and Bjarne wrote tour of C++ to try to get around this. Bjarne and others have been trying so hard. Bjarne has written textbooks. Please use my textbook, he says. I wrote it for you, and they say, what? Well, we're used to doing this. Because he wrote this textbook, so here's how you can teach.
cues.zh: 这就是为什么很多高校在 C++ 课程早期还在教 fprintf。这不算坏，但这不是 C++；Bjarne 写《Tour of C++》就是想绕开这个问题。Bjarne 和其他人一直在努力。Bjarne 写过教科书。他说，请用我的教科书，我是为你们写的。他们说，什么？嗯，我们习惯这么做了。因为他写了这本教科书，所以这就是你可以采用的教学方式。

cues.en: programming using C++, real C++, not starting with C, or starting with C++98, or the older things that have been superseded. One of the advantages of having a name for a syntax, so one of the reasons I say not just syntax too, but I call it CPP2, because if it succeeds, and it will probably fail, but if it succeeds, it also gives you a noun.
cues.zh: 用 C++ 来编程，真正的 C++，不是从 C 开始，也不是从 C++98 或已被取代的旧内容开始。给一种语法起名字的好处之一——这也是我说它不只是语法、而把它叫作 CPP2 的原因之一——是：如果它成功了（它很可能会失败，但如果成功了），它也就给了你一个名词。

cues.en: where nobody will be able to ever teach a CPP2 course and start with fprintf, because that's not in pure CPP2. And if they do, they'll use it with member functions index, because they can call it compatibly. But they can't use the old style C++98 things. They can't use null macro. They can't use zero, meaning a pointer or an integer. They can't do many of those things. They can't use naked new, where you leak things by default.
cues.zh: 这样一来，就没人能开一门 CPP2 课程却从 fprintf 开始教，因为那不在纯 CPP2 里。如果他们真要这么做，就得配合成员函数 index 来用，因为可以兼容地调用它。但他们不能用旧式 C++98 的东西。不能用 null 宏。不能用 0 来表示指针或整数。很多这类事情他们都做不了。不能用裸 new，那种默认就会泄漏资源的写法。

cues.en: with a raw pointer, an owning raw pointer. So just by having a name, my hope is that in the future when people teach courses using C++, that we will have a lever where we can make them use modern C++ because we've said what it is and we've given it a name. That's only if it succeeds, but that's the idea because otherwise I don't see any hope. If we would have brought C++ courses significantly 10x forward,
cues.zh: 用裸指针，一个拥有所有权的裸指针。所以，仅仅靠有一个名字，我希望未来当人们用 C++ 教课程时，我们有一个杠杆，可以促使他们使用现代 C++，因为我们已经说明了它是什么，并给了它一个名字。这只有在它成功的前提下才成立，但这就是想法，因为否则我看不到任何希望。如果我们能把 C++ 课程大幅推进 10 倍，

cues.en: which is part of making teaching and learning 10X better. On the current path, we would have done it by now. What other lever can we use? Perhaps this could be one. So thank you for coming to CPPCon. Thank you for coming to this talk. I hope you enjoyed the whole conference. We'll be right back here again next year. And I hope you have safe travels home wherever those travels take you. Thank you again for coming.
cues.zh: 这也是让教学和学习好上 10 倍的一部分。按目前的路径，我们本来早该做到了。我们还能用什么别的杠杆？也许这个可以是一个。感谢来参加 CPPCon。感谢来听这场演讲。希望大家享受整个大会。明年我们会再回到这里。也祝你们归途平安，无论你们去向何方。再次感谢你们的到来。
